nodes.name: API Architecture
nodes.summary: Defines RESTful API conventions for the Persuratan platform including JSON response formats (success/error), HTTP method usage (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), Zod-based input validation, session-based authentication, role-based authorization (RBAC), pagination with query parameters, and filtering.

nodes.name: Architecture Rules
nodes.summary: Mandatory architectural rules for all AI agents: strict layer separation (Page→Component→Composable→API Route→Service→Repository→Database), reuse-before-create principle, no modification of unrelated code, consistent naming conventions, TypeScript strictness with no any types, structured error handling, metadata-driven design for user-defined structures, and framework-independent domain engines.

nodes.name: Backend Architecture
nodes.summary: Describes the Nitro-based backend architecture with detailed server structure under app/server/: API route handlers (collections, components, templates, workflows, documents, files), service layer for business logic, repository layer for data access via Drizzle ORM, and five domain engines (Expression, Binding, Component, Template, Document). Includes complete HTTP request flow from route to database.

nodes.name: Database Architecture
nodes.summary: Documents the SQLite + Drizzle ORM database architecture using a hybrid approach: fixed metadata tables for Global Tables, Components, Templates, Administrations, and Documents definitions, combined with JSONB-based dynamic data storage for user-defined records. Covers naming conventions (nanoid/UUID IDs, timestamps, soft delete, JSONB columns), migration strategy via Drizzle Kit, and schema file locations.

nodes.name: Frontend Architecture
nodes.summary: Details the Nuxt 4 + Vue 3 Composition API frontend with TypeScript, Nuxt UI component library, and Tailwind CSS styling. Describes client app structure (pages, components, composables, layouts, middleware, plugins), component architecture hierarchy (Primitive→Pattern→Feature→Page), state management via Pinia and composables, and Tiptap editor integration with custom ProseMirror nodes (DynamicText, Component, Loop, Condition, PageBreak).

nodes.name: Architecture Overview
nodes.summary: High-level architecture overview describing the unified full-stack Nuxt 4 + Nitro application with three major layers (Client/Server/Data). Defines six major modules (Collections, Components, Templates, Workflows, Documents, Expression Engine) and their responsibilities. Documents the complete data flow from user action through Nuxt Page/Component → Composable → Nitro API Route → Service → Domain Engine → Repository → Drizzle ORM → SQLite.

nodes.name: Security
nodes.summary: Covers security implementation: session-based authentication using Nitro session handling with HTTP-only cookies (no JWT), role-based authorization (Administrator/Staff/Manager) with permission checks at service layer, Zod-based server-side validation as authoritative, data protection via Drizzle parameterized queries (SQL injection prevention) and Vue template escaping (XSS prevention), and environment variable-based secrets management.

nodes.name: System Context
nodes.summary: Defines the system boundary with three actors (User/Browser, Persuratan Nuxt App, SQLite Database) and one external dependency (File System for storage). In-scope features: dynamic data structures, reusable document components, template composition, administration workflows, document rendering (HTML+PDF), file management, authentication/authorization. Out-of-scope: external databases, third-party document services, external auth providers, mobile native apps, real-time collaboration.

nodes.name: Technology Stack
nodes.summary: Comprehensive technology inventory across Core (Nuxt 4, Nitro, Vue 3, TypeScript 5, Node.js 20+), Frontend (Nuxt UI, Tailwind CSS v4, Tiptap, Pinia, VueUse, TanStack Table, vee-validate, Zod, date-fns, Lucide), Backend (Drizzle ORM, SQLite, Zod, Sharp, Pino), Document Engine (Tiptap/ProseMirror, Playwright), and Testing (Vitest, Playwright E2E). Notes that naive-ui is currently installed but Nuxt UI is the design target. Package manager is pnpm.

nodes.label: Definition of Done
nodes.contentSummary: Comprehensive Definition of Done checklist for features. Covers 7 categories: Specification (10 items including requirements, domain, API, UI, acceptance), Implementation (10 items: tasks, schema, services, routes, composables, components, pages, validation, error handling, states), Verification (8 items: typecheck, lint, tests, build, API, UI, accessibility), Acceptance Criteria (all pass with evidence), UI/UX (8 states and patterns), Review (8 items: architecture, backend, frontend, UI/UX, security, performance, no CRITICAL/HIGH), and Final Check. ALL checkboxes must be checked for DONE.

nodes.label: Implementation Rules
nodes.contentSummary: 10 rules governing code implementation: Rule 1 (Read Spec First), Rule 2 (Inspect Existing Code), Rule 3 (Reuse Abstractions - search components/composables/services/repositories/schemas), Rule 4 (Don't Modify Unrelated Code), Rule 5 (Implement Incrementally), Rule 6 (Follow Architecture Rules - layer separation), Rule 7 (Follow Design System - tokens, guidelines, patterns), Rule 8 (Validate All Input - Zod server, form client), Rule 9 (Handle All States - loading/empty/error/success/disabled), Rule 10 (Write Testable Code - small functions, injectable deps).
nodes.name: implementation-rules.md

nodes.label: Review Rules
nodes.contentSummary: Rules governing implementation review. Defines 4 severity levels: CRITICAL (blocks - security, data loss, architecture violation), HIGH (blocks - missing error handling, poor UX, performance), MEDIUM (should fix - code style, edge cases), LOW (nice to have - polish, docs). Includes 6 review checklists: Requirements, Architecture, Backend, Frontend, UI/UX, Security, Performance. Defines review output format (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/Positive/Verdict) and blocking rules (CRITICAL/HIGH → CHANGES REQUIRED, MEDIUM/LOW only → APPROVED).
nodes.name: review-rules.md

nodes.label: Specification Rules
nodes.contentSummary: 10 rules governing specification writing: Rule 1 (Spec is Source of Truth), Rule 2 (Surface Ambiguity - stop and request clarification), Rule 3 (AI Must Not Invent Business Behavior), Rule 4 (Requirements Must Be Testable), Rule 5 (UI/UX Must Be Specified - pages, components, states, responsive, a11y), Rule 6 (Business Rules Explicit - ID, description, severity, validation), Rule 7 (Document Architecture Impact), Rule 8 (Identify Edge Cases), Rule 9 (Identify Dependencies), Rule 10 (Specs Must Be Reviewable).
nodes.name: specification-rules.md

nodes.label: Verification Rules
nodes.contentSummary: Rules governing implementation verification. Defines a 10-step verification pipeline: 1. Typecheck (npx nuxi typecheck - zero TS errors, no any), 2. Lint (eslint - zero errors), 3. Unit Tests (vitest - all new functions tested), 4. Integration Tests (vitest - flows tested), 5. Build (nuxi build - succeeds), 6. API Verification (endpoints, validation, auth, format), 7. UI Verification (renders, states, validation, responsive), 8. Acceptance Criteria (acceptance.md - PASS with evidence), 9. Accessibility (keyboard, focus, labels, contrast, screen reader), 10. Architecture (layer separation, boundaries, data flow). Includes verification report format template.
nodes.name: verification-rules.md

nodes.label: SDD Workflow
nodes.contentSummary: Spec-Driven Development workflow definition. Defines 11-phase pipeline: IDEA → UNDERSTAND → SPEC → REVIEW SPEC → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → REVIEW → FIX → VERIFY AGAIN → DONE. Each phase has defined Input, Activity, Rules, Output, and assigned Agent: IDEA (user request), UNDERSTAND (read docs/code), SPEC (product agent - create spec files, focus on WHAT), REVIEW SPEC (reviewer agent - completeness/ambiguity), PLAN (architect agent - task breakdown, focus on HOW), IMPLEMENT (build agent - follow tasks, incremental), VERIFY (qa agent - run checks with evidence), REVIEW (reviewer agent - compliance/quality/security), FIX (build agent - fix CRITICAL/HIGH), VERIFY AGAIN (qa re-run), DONE (all checks pass, no blocking findings).
nodes.name: workflow.md

nodes.name: GlobalTable
nodes.summary: Core entity — a metadata-driven data structure defining how data is stored, input, displayed, validated, searched, and ordered. Has status lifecycle (Draft → Published → Archived).

nodes.name: Column
nodes.summary: Field definition within a Global Table specifying data type, behavior, and UI rendering. Supports 10 types: text, number, date, time, datetime, image, select, richtext, relation, computed.

nodes.name: Record
nodes.summary: A single data entry in a Global Table, stored as a JSON document with column values as key-value pairs.

nodes.name: GlobalTable Lifecycle
nodes.summary: State machine for GlobalTable: Draft (freely modifiable) → Published (available for Components, restricted changes) → Archived (no new references, data preserved). Supports unpublish back to Draft.

transitions: Draft → Published (at least 1 column, valid names)

nodes.name: Column Type System
nodes.summary: Column type configuration system defining input components, storage formats, and type-specific configs. Includes progressive disclosure for type-specific options.

nodes.name: Auto-Generated CRUD
nodes.summary: System auto-generates full CRUD operations for each Global Table — browse, create, read, update, delete — without manual coding.

nodes.name: Dynamic Form Generation
nodes.summary: Forms are dynamically generated from column definitions — field types (text input, date picker, select, etc.) determined by column type, with computed fields displaying calculated values and relation fields showing selectable options.

nodes.name: Expression Engine
nodes.summary: External dependency for computed columns — evaluates expressions like 'harga * jumlah' to calculate values. Must prevent circular references.

nodes.summary: REST API for Global Table collection management — CRUD operations, status transitions (publish/unpublish/archive), with pagination, search, and filtering.

nodes.name: Columns API

nodes.name: Records API

nodes.name: Side Effects

SE-GT-003: Delete column with data → data loss (blocked)
SE-GT-004: Change column type → data incompatibility
SE-GT-005: Add required column → existing records need defaults

nodes.summary: Domain invariants ensuring data integrity — unique names, unique column names within table, minimum columns, protected published data, valid expressions, valid relation targets, matching record data keys, required column values.

tour.title: Project Identity & Purpose
tour.description: Understand what Persuratan is: a Spec-Driven Development platform for document composition built with Nuxt 4 full-stack. Start here to grasp the core concept: Global Table → Component → Template → Administration → Document → PDF.
tour.languageLesson: Markdown (`.md`) uses `#` for headers, `>` for blockquotes, and `**` for bold. README files are the first entry point for any project — they establish identity, purpose, and quick-start instructions.

tour.title: Technology Stack Overview
tour.description: Explore the complete technology inventory across all layers: Nuxt 4 + Nitro for full-stack, Vue 3 + TypeScript for frontend, Drizzle ORM + SQLite for data, and Tiptap for document editing. Understanding the stack prevents wrong tool assumptions.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript's `tsconfig.json` uses JSON with comments (though strict JSON forbids them). The `references` array points to Nuxt-generated configs — a pattern called 'project references' for incremental builds.

tour.title: Architecture Overview & Layer Separation
tour.description: Learn the three-layer architecture (Client → Server → Data) and the mandatory layer separation rule: Page → Component → Composable → API Route → Service → Repository → Database. This is the most critical architectural constraint.
tour.languageLesson: Architecture documents use directional arrows (→) to express flow and dependency. In TypeScript projects, layer separation prevents circular dependencies and keeps code testable.

tour.title: Backend Architecture & Request Flow
tour.description: Trace the complete HTTP request flow from Nitro API routes through services to repositories and database. Understand how five domain engines (Expression, Binding, Component, Template, Document) sit between services and repositories.
tour.languageLesson: REST API conventions use HTTP methods semantically: GET (read), POST (create), PUT (replace), PATCH (partial update), DELETE (remove). Zod validates inputs server-side — never trust client validation alone.

tour.title: Frontend Architecture & Component Hierarchy
tour.description: Understand the Nuxt 4 client structure: pages, components (Primitive → Pattern → Feature → Page), composables, layouts, and Tiptap editor integration with custom ProseMirror nodes for dynamic document content.
tour.languageLesson: Vue 3 Composition API with `<script setup>` is the standard. Components follow a hierarchy: Primitive (atomic) → Pattern (reusable组合) → Feature (business) → Page (route-level). This is analogous to Atomic Design.

tour.title: Database Architecture & Data Strategy
tour.description: Learn the hybrid database approach: fixed metadata tables for structure definitions (Global Tables, Components, Templates) combined with JSONB-based dynamic data storage for user-defined records. This enables metadata-driven design.
tour.languageLesson: SQLite with Drizzle ORM uses a 'schema-first' approach. JSONB columns store flexible user data while fixed columns store metadata. `nanoid` generates URL-safe unique IDs; `UUID` v4 for globally unique identifiers.

tour.title: Security Model & Authentication
tour.description: Explore session-based authentication with HTTP-only cookies (no JWT), role-based authorization (Administrator/Staff/Manager), and Zod-based server-side validation as the authoritative input guard.
tour.languageLesson: Session cookies are more secure than JWTs for server-rendered apps because they're automatically sent by the browser and can't be accessed via JavaScript. RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) checks permissions at the service layer.

tour.title: Design System Foundations
tour.description: Discover the 'Professional Workspace' design language: color tokens, typography scale, 4px spacing grid, elevation levels, and the component library layering (Nuxt UI → Tokens → App → Feature).
tour.languageLesson: Design tokens are named values (e.g., `--color-primary-500`) that abstract raw values. They enable theming and consistency. CSS custom properties (`--var`) make tokens runtime-switchable.

tour.title: UX Principles & Interaction Patterns
tour.description: Learn the eight interaction patterns: workspace navigation, builder canvas, command palette, form submission, destructive confirmation, drag-and-drop, split view, and step wizard. These patterns repeat across all features.
tour.languageLesson: UX patterns are reusable solutions to common interface problems. The 'command palette' (Cmd+K) pattern provides keyboard-first navigation. Responsive design uses breakpoints: sm (640px), md (768px), lg (1024px), xl (1280px).

tour.title: SDD Workflow: The Development Process
tour.description: Understand the Spec-Driven Development workflow: Requirement → SPEC → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → REVIEW → FIX → VERIFY → DONE. Every feature must follow this pipeline for quality assurance.
tour.languageLesson: SDD is a 'specification-first' methodology. Unlike agile sprints that code-then-document, SDD requires complete specifications before any implementation. The workflow files use markdown checklists and numbered phases.

tour.title: SDD Verification & Definition of Done
tour.description: Learn the 10-step verification pipeline and definition of done criteria: typecheck, lint, tests, build, acceptance criteria, and review gates. CRITICAL/HIGH findings block completion.
tour.languageLesson: Quality gates use severity levels: CRITICAL (blocks release), HIGH (must fix), MEDIUM (should fix), LOW (nice to have). The 'definition of done' is a shared checklist that prevents premature feature completion.

tour.title: Feature Spec Anatomy: Global Table
tour.description: Examine a complete feature specification. Global Table is the foundation — it defines metadata-driven data structures with columns, records, and lifecycle states (Draft → Published → Archived).
tour.languageLesson: Feature specs follow a standard anatomy: requirements (what), domain (entities + rules), business-rules (constraints), api (endpoints), ui/ux (interface), tasks (implementation), test-cases (verification), acceptance (proof).

tour.title: Global Table: API & UI Specifications
tour.description: See how the Global Table spec translates to REST endpoints (collections, columns, records APIs) and UI pages (Collections List, Workspace, Create). The UI spec includes component hierarchy and responsive behavior.
tour.languageLesson: API specs define request/response schemas with Zod. UI specs describe component trees using indentation hierarchy. UX specs map user flows with 'Given/When/Then' acceptance criteria format.

tour.title: Global Table: Tasks & Test Cases
tour.description: Review the 14 implementation tasks (schema → types → repository → service → API → composable → UI → tests) and comprehensive test cases covering unit, integration, API, and E2E levels.
tour.languageLesson: Task dependencies form a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph): TASK-001 (schema) must complete before TASK-003 (repository). Test cases use 'UT-' (unit), 'IT-' (integration), 'AT-' (API), 'ET-' (E2E) prefixes for categorization.

tour.title: Expression Engine: Domain & Parsing
tour.description: Explore the Expression Engine — a pure domain engine that parses and evaluates mathematical/string/conditional expressions. It uses a Tokenizer → Parser → Evaluator pipeline with AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) nodes.
tour.languageLesson: An AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) represents code as a tree structure. Tokenization splits `'price * qty'` into tokens [`price`, `*`, `qty`]. Parsing builds the tree. Evaluation walks the tree to compute results. This is compiler theory applied to runtime expressions.

tour.title: Expression Engine: Implementation & Tests
tour.description: See the 8 implementation tasks in dependency order and 26 test cases. The engine exposes 3 API endpoints: validate (syntax check), evaluate (compute), and resolve (dynamic tokens).
tour.languageLesson: Expression engines must handle edge cases: division by zero, undefined variables, circular references, and nesting depth limits. The 'resolve' endpoint handles dynamic token resolution — converting user-facing tokens to internal references.

tour.title: Component Feature: Reusable Document Blocks
tour.description: Understand Components — reusable document blocks with dynamic tokens, data requirements, and Tiptap content model. Components have their own lifecycle (Draft → Published → Archived) and support single/collection modes.
tour.languageLesson: Tiptap is a headless rich-text editor built on ProseMirror. Custom nodes (DynamicText, Loop, Condition) extend the editor for document composition. The 'data requirements' pattern declares what data a component needs — enabling validation before use.

tour.title: Component: UI Builder & Implementation
tour.description: Explore the Component Builder's three-panel layout (Insert | Canvas | Properties) and the 12 implementation tasks. The builder uses command palette-style insertion and drag-and-drop reordering.
tour.languageLesson: Three-panel layouts are common in IDEs and design tools: left (insertion/navigation), center (canvas/workspace), right (properties/inspector). This pattern maximizes screen real estate while keeping tools accessible.

tour.title: Template Feature: Document Composition
tour.description: Templates compose Components into document blueprints with data bindings, loops, and conditions. The Template Builder adds a Data Panel for binding configuration alongside the three-panel layout.
tour.languageLesson: Data binding connects template variables to data sources (administration, global-table, manual, expression, system). Loops iterate over record collections. Conditions control section visibility. These are document-as-code patterns.

tour.title: Administration & Document Features
tour.description: Discover how Administrations orchestrate Templates into workflows, and how Documents are generated instances with HTML storage and PDF rendering. These are the final steps in the data flow pipeline.
tour.languageLesson: State machines govern entity lifecycles. Administrations have Steps (sequential tasks), Instances (running executions), and InstanceSteps (per-step state). Documents transition from Generating → Generated/Failed — a common async job pattern.

tour.title: Render Engine & PDF Generation
tour.description: The Render Engine is the final pipeline stage: it resolves all bindings, evaluates expressions, renders Tiptap content to HTML, and generates PDFs via Playwright. It's the bridge between templates and output.
tour.languageLesson: Playwright (normally for E2E testing) is repurposed for PDF generation — it renders HTML in a real browser engine, ensuring pixel-perfect output. This 'browser-as-a-service' pattern avoids wkhtmltopdf's limitations.

tour.title: Specification Template: Creating New Features
tour.description: Study the `_template/` directory — the canonical structure for writing new feature specifications. Every new feature must produce these 8 documents following the same patterns established by existing specs.
tour.languageLesson: Templates use placeholder patterns: `REQ-XXX-NNN` for requirement IDs, `[resource]` for API paths, `[Entity]` for domain classes. The template ensures consistency — every feature spec has the same structure, making codebase navigation predictable.

tour.title: Full Data Flow: End-to-End Pipeline
tour.description: Trace the complete data flow: User creates Global Table → defines Columns → adds Records → creates Component with dynamic tokens → assembles Template with bindings → runs Administration workflow → generates Document → renders PDF.
tour.languageLesson: Metadata-driven design means the system's behavior is defined by data (column types, component tokens, template bindings) rather than hardcoded logic. This enables users to create new data structures without writing code — the system adapts automatically.

tour.title: Configuration & Project Setup
tour.description: Review the build configuration: pnpm workspace setup, Nuxt config, TypeScript references, and the .opencode configuration for AI-assisted development. These files define how the project builds and runs.
tour.languageLesson: pnpm workspaces enable monorepo management with strict dependency isolation. Nuxt config (`nuxt.config.ts`) uses `defineNuxtConfig()` with TypeScript autocomposition. The `postinstall` script runs `nuxt prepare` to generate types.
